procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Judicature at Allahabad issued a Judgment and Order on 12.12.2023 in CRLA Nos. 2467, 996, 801, 1155 and 467 of 2021. The bail order dated 12.12.2023 was passed in other connected Criminal Appeal No. 996 of 2021, Criminal Appeal No. 801 of 201, Criminal Appeal No. 1155 of 2021 and Criminal Appeal No. 467 of 2021.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Appellants approached the Supreme Court challenging the High Court's Judgment and Order dated 12.12.2023. The Supreme Court allowed the appeals.

decision.conviction_status: No observation made on the merits of the appeals against conviction, to be considered on its own merits in the pending appeals.
decision.sentence_status: The order suspending the sentence and granting bail is set aside; bail is cancelled.
directions: The impugned order is set aside.
The bail granted to the private respondent in all these appeals stands cancelled.
The appellants shall surrender before the trial Court for the purpose of their committal to judicial custody within a period of four days.
In case of their failure to surrender as ordered, the private respondents who are convicts shall be re-arrested and committed to custody.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the High Court was justified in suspending the sentences of the convicted respondents and granting them bail on the basis of their offer to pay monetary compensation to the victim.
appellant_arguments: The appellant-victim implicitly argued against the High Court's order by appealing it. The Supreme Court's reaction suggests the appellant's position was that suspending a sentence in exchange for a monetary payment was improper and unjust.
respondent_arguments: The private respondents (convicts) offered to pay ₹25 lakhs to the victim for her treatment as a condition for the suspension of their sentences.
They argued that since they had fulfilled their part by depositing the offered amount, they should be released on bail.
They also noted that the hearing of their appeal in the High Court was likely to take a significant amount of time.
The State respondent (represented by the AGA) had no objection to the prayer made by the appellant in the Supreme Court.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The provided text does not contain the binding legal rule.
obiter: Regarding the merits of the appeals by the party respondents against their conviction, the court shall not be understood to have held or made any observation as it is a matter to be considered on its own merits in the pending appeals.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The Supreme Court's conscience was shocked by the High Court's order. The High Court failed in its duty to objectively assess the matter and record sufficient reasons for suspending the sentence and granting bail. The only factor that appeared to weigh with the High Court was the absence of any allegation that the respondents had misused their liberty when previously on bail, which is an insufficient justification on its own. The grant of bail was not appropriate in the first place, given the very serious nature of the charges against the accused.
legal_tests_applied: An appellate court is duty-bound to objectively assess the matter and to record reasons for the conclusion that the case warrants suspension of execution of sentence and grant of bail.

While bail, once granted, should not be cancelled mechanically without supervening circumstances, it can be cancelled where the grant of bail was not appropriate in the first place given the very serious nature of the charges against the accused which disentitles him for bail and thus cannot be justified.
policy_considerations: The court's conscience was shocked by the High Court's order, indicating a fundamental concern for justice in the bail process.
There is a need to prevent the inappropriate granting of bail, especially when the charges against the accused are of a very serious nature.
